environment: Source /opt/openfoam10/etc/bashrc; CUDA 13.1 was used, UGKWP_CUDA_ARCH=sm_89. Execute GPU work serially. Keep fresh output directories.

variables.CHMT_BASE: accepted layer-two CHMT binary (CPU solid conduction)
variables.CHT_BASE: directory containing accepted layer-one CHT binary (CPU solid conduction)
variables.CAND: directory containing candidate CHMT and CHT binaries
variables.ARCHIVE: CUDA archive from candidate CHT build

commands: python3 $R/validation/gpu_coupled_pipeline/layer2_native.py --baseline $CHMT_BASE --baseline-role 'Accepted layer two; CPU solid conduction' --candidate $CAND/CHMT --source $B --cases-root $C --inspector $E/layer2-cpu-baseline/bin/checkpoint_material --work $E/native --scenarios thermal single diffusion dry receding
python3 $R/validation/gpu_coupled_pipeline/layer1.py --baseline $CHT_BASE --candidate $CAND --work $E/cht --cases cht-contact cht-mixture cht-pure cht-wall cht-ode cht-wallfunction
additional_checks: Run compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --leak-check full --error-exitcode 99 on sparse-test, material_backend_transaction and fresh native CHT/CHMT cases. Check numerical parity after sanitizer execution.
Run layer3_cht_restart.py on baseline and candidate contact, mixture and wall cases, then compare the restarted output fields strictly with layer1.compare_fields.
Build material_backend_transaction with the production MaterialBackend object and UGKWP_GAS_SPECIES=2; layer3_kernels.sh independently checks thermal constitutive math for Ns=2 and Ns=3.
timing_scope: Native process timing includes startup and normal output, with one warmup plus five alternating pairs. Strong conduction timing includes properties, assembly and nonlinear iteration in a resident owner, with one warmup plus five repeated solves per binary. The latter is not an alternating full-application benchmark.
production_scope: Shared operators for the existing CHT and CHMT applications. Verification fixtures do not introduce production dispatch by case or mesh. gasUGKP remains a distinct pure-flow application.
